examples.purpose: A portfolio card, the guide's In context: the screen works out each part's share and passes the same list, in the same order, to the track and the legend, so their colours match. The track keeps its default Senary gold and is named by its spoken name; each MetricLegendItem carries Senary and its slice's emphasis (High, Medium, Low), so its dot takes its slice's colour.
examples.jsx:
<Card>
  <VStack>
    <Text text="Portfolio mix" />
    <Text text="₹4,20,000 invested" />
    <SegmentedTrack
      segments={[
        { key: 'Equity', value: 60 },
        { key: 'Debt', value: 25 },
        { key: 'Cash', value: 15 },
      ]}
      accessibilityLabel="Portfolio mix: equity 60%, debt 25%, cash 15%"
    />
    <VStack>
      <MetricLegendItem label="Equity" value="60%" modes={{ 'Appearance / DataViz': 'Senary', 'Emphasis / DataViz': 'High' }} />
      <MetricLegendItem label="Debt" value="25%" modes={{ 'Appearance / DataViz': 'Senary', 'Emphasis / DataViz': 'Medium' }} />
      <MetricLegendItem label="Cash" value="15%" modes={{ 'Appearance / DataViz': 'Senary', 'Emphasis / DataViz': 'Low' }} />
    </VStack>
  </VStack>
</Card>

props.name: segments
props.description: Each part's value sets its width as a share of the total (flex: value; a missing value counts as 1; 0 keeps a 1 px sliver). An empty list draws an empty, transparent 24 px track; leaving segments out draws three equal default slices. Declared: Data-driven segment list. Used when no `children` slot is provided. Defaults to three equal segments which receive per-index Emphasis defaults (`High`, `Medium`, `Low`).

props.name: children
props.description: Slot for fully custom segment children. Each top-level child is treated as one segment. The parent injects per-index Emphasis defaults and the shared `modes`, while child-level `modes` overrides win.

props.name: modes
props.description: Design token modes for theming (e.g. `{ 'Color Mode': 'Light' }`).

props.name: segmentStyle
props.description: Style applied to every segment (data-driven mode only).

props.name: accessibilityLabel
props.description: The track's spoken name. On the web the track is a group (role group) named by it. Declared: Accessibility label announced for the whole distribution row.

props.name: SegmentedTrack.Segment
props.description: A static sub-component of SegmentedTrack. Its own props: value, color, modes, style, accessibilityLabel.

modes.name: Appearance / DataViz
modes.description: A track with no modes has Senary gold slices (206,161,90 / 232,188,122 / 253,232,201 at High, Medium, Low), as in Figma, not the collection's default Primary (purple). An appearance recolours every slice. Declared: A token collection SegmentedTrack reads (the package's FIGMA_COMPONENT_MODES). When modes leave it unset, the resolver uses the collection's default mode. Package docs: Each segment resolves its color through the `dataViz/bg` token, which cascades through `Emphasis / DataViz` and `Appearance / DataViz`. Pass `modes` per segment (or override `Appearance / DataViz` at the parent level via `modes`) to retheme the row without touching colors directly.

modes.name: Color Mode
modes.description: A token collection SegmentedTrack reads (the package's FIGMA_COMPONENT_MODES). When modes leave it unset, the resolver uses the collection's default mode.

modes.name: Emphasis / DataViz
modes.description: Set on each slice by its position: High, Medium, Low, then repeating, as checked in Light (the guide shows Light only). An Emphasis / DataViz on the track itself is overwritten; a segment's own modes win. Declared: A token collection SegmentedTrack reads (the package's FIGMA_COMPONENT_MODES). When modes leave it unset, the resolver uses the collection's default mode. Package docs: Each segment resolves its color through the `dataViz/bg` token, which cascades through `Emphasis / DataViz` and `Appearance / DataViz`.

slots.name: children
slots.description: Slot for fully custom segment children. Each top-level child is treated as one segment. The parent injects per-index Emphasis defaults and the shared `modes`, while child-level `modes` overrides win.
